surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Mintyukov scores twice as the Ducks beat the Oilers
paras: Pavel Mintyukov had a Gordie Howe hat trick: a goal, an assist and a fight. Mintyukov, who scores in about 1 game in 13, scored twice. Cutter Gauthier got the scoring started for the Ducks on the power play midway through the first, his fourth straight game with a goal. Kasperi Kapanen and Mintyukov dropped the gloves late in the period. Evan Bouchard tied it 1-1 for Edmonton on the power play with 19 seconds left in the period. It was a busy second period. Connor McDavid put the Oilers ahead 2-1 shorthanded early in the period. Mintyukov scored later in the period and again less than three minutes later to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 3-2 lead. Beckett Sennecke made it 4-2 late in the second. He scored again on the power play early in the third to make it 5-2, and that one stood up as the winner. Kapanen cut Anaheim’s lead to 5-3 on the power play with less than four minutes left. With the goalie pulled and 45 seconds left, Leon Draisaitl made it 5-4, but the Ducks held on. Two players had three-point nights: Mintyukov with two goals and an assist, and Sennecke with two goals and an assist.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Oilers hit two posts and still lost. Laurent Brossoit made 23 saves for the Ducks, and Matt Tomkins allowed five goals on 21 shots.

Vasily Podkolzin was thrown out with a game misconduct midway through the first. Noah Warren took three penalties on his own. The Ducks improved to 8-7-1, fourth in the Pacific, while the Oilers dropped to 11-3-3, slipping out of first in the NHL.
